definition: A bright star very close to the North celestial pole.
intuition: Because it lies near Earth’s extended rotation axis, Polaris appears nearly fixed while surrounding stars trace circles.
misconceptions: Polaris is not exactly at the celestial pole.
Polaris is not the brightest night-sky star.
takeaway: Its altitude is approximately the observer’s northern latitude.

source.section: Looking Out from a Spinning, Round Earth
